To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Ozone pretreatment increased biodegradability and improved biological treatment of ECF bleached kraft effluents, (2) Ozone pretreated effluences could be treated with lower specific oxygen uptake rates, (3) Ozone pretreatments produced better effluent quality than post-treatments, (4) Ozone pretretment increased the efficiency of post-treatment, and (5) Ozone pretreaments were more cost-effective than post-treat

ozone pretreatment increased the biodegradability of the effluents by 10-24%, but had no effect on biological activity during treatment, and that ozone pretreatment was more effective than post-treatment for the removal of recalcitrent organics from the effluents.
the combination of ozonation with biological treatment of ECF bleached kraft effluent was effective in removing recalcitrant organics, and that pre-ozonation was more effective than post-ozonaton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the removal of recalcitrent organic matter in bleaching effluents from eucalypt pulp mills.
the treatment of effluent from the bleaching of kraft pulp, using a combination of chemical (ozone) and biological treatment.
the removal of organic matter from bleached kraft effluents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ozone pretreatment of effluent E2 resulted in an improved effluent quality and a lower biological activity.
the combined chemical-biological process is more efficient in removing recalcitrant compounds than biological treatment alone.
ozone pretreatment can be beneficial to subsequent biological treatment of bleaching effluent, but that the benefits are not universal and may be dependent on the nature of the effluent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pre-ozonation is a more effective treatment than post-ozonaton.
the combined treatment of ozone-biological treatment of bleached kraft effluents is a promising alternative to biological treatment alone.
the combined chemical and biological treatment is an efficient way to remove organic matter from pulp mill effluents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timing of ozone addition relative to biological treatment is an important consideration in designing combined treatment processes.
ozone pretreatment is a more effective way to enhance biological treatment of bleaching effluent than ozone post-treatment.
ozone pretreatment is more effective than post-treatment, especially for effluents with a high content of recalcitrance organic matter, such as lignin.
